name: Polar sea ice
summary: Arctic sea ice 1.77M km² and Antarctic 1.36M km² below average on 17 Nov; neither at a record low
state: On 17 Nov Arctic sea-ice extent was 9.00 million km², about 1.77 million km² below the 1981–2010 average and the third lowest for the date, with extent dipping slightly between 16 and 17 Nov (NSIDC). Antarctic extent was 14.53 million km², about 1.36 million km² below average and the fourth lowest for the date. Both are past the −1.0 million km² Watch line, and neither pole is at a record low.
for_you: Low sea ice is a long-term climate indicator with no immediate effect on daily life in the UK. It tends to add to ocean warming and can affect weather patterns over time.
rubric_hit: Watch: Arctic -1.77M km² and Antarctic -1.36M km² below the -1.0M km² line; no record low for date

sources.title: NSIDC — Sea Ice Index v4 daily extent

why: Sea ice reflects sunlight and regulates ocean circulation; record lows accelerate warming.
drivers: Air and ocean temperatures, winds, season.

rubric.alert: Either pole at a record low for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Arctic and Antarctic extent anomalies both above −1.0 million km² vs 1981–2010.
